title: Protect, inform, sell: the three jobs of your package
course_title: Product Packaging & Branding for Small Producers

say: Protect, inform, sell: the three jobs of your package.
This is the video for Module 1 of Product Packaging and Branding.
Packaging is the silent salesperson that stands beside your product when you are not there. It has three jobs, in this order.
First, protect. Keep out air, moisture, dust, light and ants, and survive a hot bus, a dusty market table and a rider's box in the rain. If the package fails to protect, nothing else matters.

panel.heading: Every package has three jobs
items: Protect: keep out air, moisture, ants, dust
Inform: what it is, weight, maker, dates
Sell: name, logo, colours, a short promise

say: Second, inform. Tell the buyer what it is, how much is inside, what it is made from, who made it, and when to use it by. Your batch number lets you trace any complaint.

panel.heading: Every package has three jobs

say: Third, sell. Buyers often decide in a few seconds, so the front of your pack must say clearly what the product is and why it is worth the price.

say: Amaka sells chin chin in thin nylon bags with no label. Customers complain it goes soft in three days, and shops will not stock it because there is no name or date.

card.title: From nylon bag to sealed pouch

say: She sells about 50 bags a week at 500 naira, and each nylon bag costs her about 20 naira.

card.title: From nylon bag to sealed pouch

say: She switches to food-grade stand-up pouches with a zip, sealed with a small impulse heat sealer. That is about 120 naira per pack. She adds a sticker with her brand, weight, ingredients, phone number, batch number and best-before date.

card.title: From nylon bag to sealed pouch

say: She raises the price to 700 naira to cover the cost.
The chin chin stays crisp, two shops agree to stock it, and her profit per pack goes up. Protection came first, information second, selling power third.

say: These three words are not the same. Your brand is the name, look and promise people remember, and the reputation you earn.

panel.heading: Brand, package and label
right: PDP: the front panel buyers see

say: The package is the physical container: the jar, lid, pouch or box. The label carries the printed information and design. The front that faces the buyer is called the principal display panel, or P D P.

say: Most plastic containers show a number from 1 to 7 in a small triangle. It tells you the plastic type. Number 1, P E T, suits cold drinks like zobo, but not very hot filling.

panel.heading: Read the number in the triangle
items: 1 PET: water, juice and zobo bottles
2 HDPE: liquid soap and detergent bottles
5 PP: food tubs, cream jars, bottle caps
Glass: honey, oils, pepper paste; breaks
Laminated pouch: snacks, spices, powders

say: Number 2, H D P E, is strong and suits soaps and detergents.

say: Never reuse a bottle that held chemicals, fuel, insecticide or detergent for food or cosmetics.

panel.heading: Three rules for a safe packing area

cards.d: Never reuse bottles that held chemicals, fuel, insecticide or detergent for food or cosmetics.
Washed hands, hair covered, a covered table away from animals. Wipe the rim before closing.
Keep fingers off the sealing bar. Unplug after use. Never use a damaged cable or plug.

say: Pack in a clean, covered area away from animals, with hands washed and hair covered. Wipe the rim before closing, so the seal grips.

say: Heat sealers and hot fills can burn. Keep fingers away from the sealing bar, unplug the sealer after use, keep it away from children, and do not overload one extension socket.

say: To remember. Protect, inform, sell, in that order. Know the difference between brand, package and label. Test your name, and choose food-grade containers.
And test samples with your real product for a week before you order in bulk. The best label cannot rescue the wrong container.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Protect first, inform second, sell third
Brand, package and label are different things
Test names for meaning, spelling and availability
Ask for food-grade containers; check the code
Test sample containers for a week first
